howItWorks.fundingTitle: How the funding works, in brief

fundingSteps.d: You apply to your state's own program on its own website. bina cannot apply on your behalf and cannot influence the decision — but we tell you exactly what to put where, and what your numbers will be, before you start.

fundingSteps.t: bina is already on the approved side
fundingSteps.d: The part most families worry about — whether the school they picked is allowed — is already settled in these five states. That is the whole reason this page exists for your state and not for others.
We publish the remainder on your state's page rather than letting you discover it at the paperwork stage. It is a monthly figure, and there is $1,500 off for each additional child.

faq.q: Is bina a homeschool program or a school?
faq.a: A school. Your child has a class, a timetable, certified teachers and report cards — the same structure as an in-person school, delivered live online. Most state programs list us under online or nonpublic schooling rather than homeschool curriculum, and we tell you exactly which category applies in your state before you apply.

faq.q: What if my state approves me for less than the full amount?
faq.a: You pay the difference. We show you the number before you commit, and we offer quarterly and yearly plans plus $1,500 off per additional child, so the gap is a monthly figure you can plan around.

faq.q: What if my application is turned down, or the window has closed?
faq.a: You are not stuck with a school you never chose. Families join bina and pay directly while an application is pending, and we time your start around your funding date once it is confirmed. Nothing about enrolling forces you to wait for the state.

faq.q: My child is neurodivergent or has an IEP. Does that change anything?
faq.a: Often in your favor — several states fund more per child for special needs. On our side, small classes and a Family Success team are the whole point; parents of neurodivergent children are a large share of our families, and they say so in the reviews on this page.

faq.q: Can I use ESA money for bina alongside other things?
faq.a: That depends on your state's rules and your award, not on us. Tuition for an online school is an approved category in the states listed here; whether there is room left over for other purchases is a question for your state's handbook, and we will point you at the exact page.

faq.q: We live in a state that isn't listed here. Can we still join bina?
faq.a: Yes — families join bina from all over the world without any state funding. These pages cover only the states where we can accept your state's money today; we are working on more, and new programs are approved most years. Email us your state and we will tell you straight where it stands and let you know if that changes.

states.pill: Arizona ESA · bina is an approved provider
states.h1: Arizona families can use ESA funds toward a bina education
states.intro: Arizona's Empowerment Scholarship Account gives your family $7,000–$8,000 per child, per year to spend on approved education — and bina is an approved provider. You spend it through ClassWallet, the state pays us directly, and you cover the remainder. Arizona has no annual deadline, so this is a decision you can make in any month of the year.
gate: bina is an approved Arizona ESA provider
states.coverTitle: Arizona's own handbook approves what bina is
states.coverBody: The ESA handbook lists “tuition or fees for a nonpublic online learning program” as an approved expense — the exact category bina sits in. You are not hoping a reviewer stretches a rule.
states.timingTitle: Arizona is open all year, and the date you sign moves your money
states.timingBody: There is no annual deadline — applications run year-round. Funding quarters start Jun 1, Sep 1, Dec 1 and Mar 1, and your quarter is set by your contract-signing date, so signing with bina earlier puts you in an earlier funding quarter. Of the five states on this site, Arizona is the easiest one to start in mid-year.

faq.q: Is bina really an approved Arizona ESA expense, or are we hoping a reviewer agrees?
faq.a: It is written into the state's own handbook. Arizona lists “tuition or fees for a nonpublic online learning program” as an approved expense, and ClassWallet has a built-in category for it. You are not relying on a reviewer stretching a rule.

faq.q: $7,000–$8,000 doesn't cover $10,769. What do I actually pay?
faq.a: The difference — roughly $230 to $315 a month, before $1,500 off for each additional child. We put your exact number in writing before you commit. Awards for a child with special needs are higher in Arizona, sometimes much higher, which can close the gap entirely.

faq.q: Can we start mid-year?
faq.a: Yes, and Arizona is the best state on this site for it. There is no annual deadline; your funding quarter is set by the date you sign, with cutoffs on Jun 1, Sep 1, Dec 1 and Mar 1. Sign earlier, get funded sooner.

faq.q: How long does approval take?
faq.a: Up to 30 days. You pre-register with the Arizona Department of Education, then set up ClassWallet and link your bank. We tell you what to have ready so none of that stalls.

states.pill: Utah Fits All · bina is an approved provider
states.h1: Utah families can use Utah Fits All funds toward a bina education
states.intro: The Utah Fits All Scholarship awards $8,000 per child, per year, paid into your Odyssey account to spend on approved education — and bina is an approved provider. Awards are limited and the window is once a year, so the useful thing to know today is when it opens and what to have ready.
gate: bina is an approved Utah Fits All provider
states.coverTitle: $8,000 covers most of a bina year
states.coverBody: Utah pays the scholarship into your Odyssey account and you spend it on approved education, including tuition at an online school like bina.
states.timingTitle: The next window opens Mar 1, 2027 — and awards are limited
states.timingBody: Utah law sets the same dates every year: Mar 1 for returning students and their siblings, Apr 1 for new students, and the portal closes May 1. The 2026–27 window closed on May 1, 2026, so the next one runs Mar 1 – May 1, 2027. Not everyone who applies is funded, so families who don't want to lose a year start at bina now and apply the day the window opens — we keep your paperwork ready for it.

faq.q: The window is closed. Is there any point talking to you now?
faq.a: Yes — that is exactly when it helps. The next window is Mar 1 – May 1, 2027, awards are limited, and the families who get funded are the ones who applied in the first days with clean paperwork. We get you ready for it, and plenty of families start at bina in the meantime and pay directly.

faq.q: Are Utah Fits All awards guaranteed if I qualify?
faq.a: No. Every Utah K–12 family is eligible, but the money runs out — awards are announced in mid-June and you accept by the end of June. We plan your bina start around your notification date rather than assuming the award, so a no from the state never leaves you without a school.

faq.q: $8,000 against $10,769 — what is left for me?
faq.a: About $230 a month, before $1,500 off for each additional child. Utah Fits All is the largest base award of the five states on this site.

faq.q: Does bina being outside Utah — or outside the US — disqualify us?
faq.a: No. Utah's statute explicitly contemplates a private school not physically located in Utah, and you spend the scholarship through the Odyssey marketplace where bina is a provider.

states.coverTitle: This one is a refund, not a wallet
states.coverBody: Idaho does not pay bina directly. You enroll, you pay tuition, you submit the receipts — and the state returns up to $5,000 per child as a refundable credit or an advance payment. We produce the receipts you need without you having to ask twice.
states.timingTitle: The next window runs Jan 15 – Mar 15, 2027 — first come, first served
states.timingBody: You apply through your Idaho Taxpayer Access Point (TAP) account between Jan 15 and Mar 15, 2027. The money is handed out in the order applications arrive, and from 2027 priority goes first to families who received the credit the year before, then to households at or below 300% of the federal poverty level. Both 2026 windows have closed. Families joining now enroll and pay directly, and we have your receipts and enrollment letter ready for January.

faq.q: Does Idaho pay bina, or pay me?
faq.a: You. This one is a tax credit, not a school account — you pay bina, submit the receipts, and Idaho returns up to $5,000 per child as a refundable credit or an advance payment. We give you the itemized invoice, enrollment letter and accreditation details every time you need them.

faq.q: So I have to fund the whole year myself first?
faq.a: You fund it and claim it back — and you can apply for the advance payment rather than waiting for a refund. We have quarterly and yearly plans, and $1,500 off per additional child, so the cash-flow shape is something we work out with you on the call.

faq.q: Both 2026 windows closed. Have we missed it?
faq.a: For 2026, yes. The next window is Jan 15 – Mar 15, 2027. Because the claim is built on receipts, starting at bina now does not cost you eligibility — it gives you the receipts. It is first come, first served, so being documented and ready in January matters more in Idaho than anywhere else.

faq.q: Who gets priority in 2027?
faq.a: Families who received the credit the year before, then households at or below 300% of the federal poverty level, then everyone else in the order applications arrive.

faq.q: Up to $5,000 — what is my real cost?
faq.a: About $480 a month net of the credit, before $1,500 off for each additional child. A child with a disability qualifies for up to $7,500, which brings it down further.

Tell us you're in Wyoming and you will hear from us the day it is published — before the window, not after it closes.

states.pill: New Hampshire EFA · bina is an approved provider
states.h1: New Hampshire families can use EFA funds toward a bina education
states.intro: New Hampshire's Education Freedom Account gives your family about $5,000 per child, per year through ClassWallet — and bina is an approved provider. The income cap was removed in 2025, so every New Hampshire family is eligible, and applications run all year. Enrollment is capped statewide at 12,500 students, which is the one reason to move early.
gate: bina is an approved New Hampshire EFA provider
states.coverTitle: A rolling program, paid in four installments
states.coverBody: The EFA accepts applications all year and pays into your ClassWallet account in September, November, January and April — which lines up with how bina bills, so you are never asked for money the state hasn't sent yet.
states.timingTitle: Rolling all year — but Jul 15, 2027 is the deadline that decides your award size
states.timingBody: For a full 2027–28 award your application must be complete and verified by Jul 15, 2027, so send your documents by Jul 1 to leave time for verification. Miss it and you can still get a prorated award for the year already underway, right through the end of February. Decisions take about 30 days, or up to two months if the state asks for more paperwork, and funds arrive in four installments — September, November, January and April. The sensible order is to talk to us first and apply with your bina numbers in hand.

faq.q: I thought the EFA had an income limit.
faq.a: It did — until 2025, when SB 295 removed the 350% federal-poverty-level cap. Every New Hampshire K–12 family is now eligible. Enrollment is capped statewide at 12,500 students, so early is better, but your income is no longer the question.

faq.q: Can we apply mid-year?
faq.a: Yes. The EFA is rolling all year. Apply and be verified by Jul 15 for a full award for the coming year; after that you can still get a prorated award for the year already underway, right through the end of February.

faq.q: When does the money arrive, and does it match how bina bills?
faq.a: Funds land in your ClassWallet account in four installments — September, November, January and April. That lines up with how bina bills, so you are not asked for money the state hasn't sent yet.

faq.q: About $5,000 against $10,769 — what is my share?
faq.a: About $480 a month, before $1,500 off for each additional child. We put your exact figure in writing before you commit.

faq.q: How long does a decision take?
faq.a: About 30 days, or up to two months if the state asks for more documents — which is why we suggest talking to us first and applying with your bina numbers and paperwork already in hand.
